title: FDA: Fourier Domain Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation
venue: CVPR 2020 (from memory; the arXiv page lists no venue)
mechanism: Replace the low-frequency Fourier amplitude of a labelled source image with that of an unlabelled target image; the alignment needs no training.
adaptation: Targets: the pool's 1,152 multi half-cells and CSIR cells (E1 is 101 CSIR, 58 half-cut). Small beta 0.005 to 0.02 so only illumination profile and contrast move; masks unchanged. Training time only.
min_experiment: Arm: house + FDA (beta 0.01, p 0.5), 5 seeds. Baseline: house and PF. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU; test crack IoU must not fall by more than 0.01. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.03.
evidence: R: state of the art on synthetic-to-real segmentation benchmarks at the time (abstract). No EL evidence.
prior_overlap: Not closed: section 5 lists UDA-style methods aimed at E1 as open. Inference-time intensity normalisation (fail) is a different mechanism.
